findings.title: Export fence records on the current device rather than the tensor device
findings.scenario: Create or import tensor on device 0, enqueue its legacy-stream write, switch current device to 1, export to a nonblocking device-0 consumer stream. Event creation and record run on device 1; the device-0 consumer waits on that unrelated event, so it may read before device-0 writes finish.
findings.fix: Guard event creation/record with the tensor device and restore the caller device, or explicitly refuse a current-device mismatch before exporting.
findings.evidence_class: Source reasoning from verified primary API semantics; unchanged core export source traced with CPU CUDA-call replacements. No GPU witness claimed.
findings.prior_art: DLPack Python/Array API stream handoff; NVIDIA CUDA 12.6 device/event semantics

findings.title: from_dlpack still documents the removed bounded shutdown wait
findings.scenario: User reads from_dlpack help and expects the exit wait to end after _DLPACK_SHUTDOWN_WAIT_S, but FIX3 waits for quiescence without a bound.
findings.fix: Update the public docstring to describe the diagnostic delay and unbounded wait.
findings.prior_art: CPython 3.12 atexit and lifecycle documentation; no new algorithm

findings.title: Core import ignores cudaGetDevice failure and consumes the capsule
findings.scenario: With no usable CUDA device, cudaGetDevice returns cudaErrorNoDevice and does not supply an ordinal; cur remains initialized to 0. A zero-size device-0 capsule is accepted and renamed used_dltensor. Likewise a failed query from an earlier CUDA error is treated as a successful device-0 query.
findings.fix: Check cudaGetDevice return; raise a named RuntimeError before Storage construction or capsule renaming.
findings.evidence_class: CPU native reproduction using verbatim core import/storage source and real CUDA runtime; no GPU/data dereference
findings.prior_art: NVIDIA CUDA 12.6 cudaGetDevice error semantics; DLPack ownership handoff

findings.title: synchronize omits the already-present synchronous CUDA error slot
findings.scenario: A launch is refused synchronously (for example invalid configuration), so there is no failed work queued on the stream but the calling host thread last-error slot is nonzero. If subsequent device queries and stream sync succeed, synchronize returns success without inspecting that slot.
findings.fix: Capture the calling thread existing CUDA error on entry, drain safely, and raise a named error even if every stream synchronization succeeds.
findings.evidence_class: Source reasoning from CUDA error-slot versus stream-completion APIs; actual-source CPU call tracing only. Real-CUDA witness pending; no GPU reproduction claimed.
findings.prior_art: NVIDIA CUDA 12.6 cudaPeekAtLastError/cudaGetLastError and cudaStreamSynchronize semantics
